$about: Hand-marked Persian reference corpus for lip-sync. This is INPUT data, not
measurement output: every syllable break and phoneme here was marked by hand,
and nothing in src/ produced any of it. That is the whole point — the library
currently has no ground truth to be measured against, so `speak('سلام')` can
be neither right nor wrong, only unexamined.
Structure is words → syllables → phonemes, three levels deep, because all
three matter to lip-sync and each is a separate claim that can be checked:
word boundaries decide where the mouth rests, syllable count decides how long
the utterance is, and phonemes decide which shapes appear.
Nothing here is derived from the other levels, so test/speech-corpus.test.mjs
can cross-check them: every syllable must have exactly one vowel (true of
Persian by construction), and the phonemes must concatenate back to `roman`.
A hand-marked file with no such check would rot silently.
$transcription: Romanization: â a e i o u for vowels; š č ž x q ɣ ʔ for the consonants without
a plain Latin letter; y and v are the glides. Long/short is not marked because
modern Persian does not contrast it phonemically.
Register: careful standard Persian, as written. Colloquial Tehrani differs and
differs a lot — می‌خواهم is /mixâham/ here and /mixâm/ in speech, which is 3
syllables against 2. Marked as written because that is what a driver passes to
`speak()`; where the two diverge sharply the entry carries a `colloquial` note
and the gap tool reports both.
$caveat: These annotations were marked by hand and are NOT a native speaker's. Three
have since been checked against Wiktionary's Iranian Persian IPA and carry a
`source` field; the rest have not, and remain one person's reading.
An earlier version of this note claimed 'the four entries carrying colloquial
notes'. There were two. That error is left recorded here rather than quietly
removed, because it is the argument for the check: a hand-marked file's own
description of its weak points was itself wrong, and nothing caught it until
What the lexicon check changed: ستاره and متشکرم were confirmed exactly as
marked, so the two entries flagged as least trustworthy were in fact fine.
What it found instead was the opposite defect — three entries whose formal
marking is correct but which reduce hard in Tehrani speech and carried no
`colloquial` note at all. Unverified ground truth was wrong in a different
place than the person who wrote it guessed.
Still outstanding, and NOT resolvable by more lexicon lookups: whether the
written register is the right reference at all for a children's character,
and the stress placement, which no entry here marks. Review by a Persian
speaker remains the cheapest improvement available to this file.

items.note: the /e/ of ke- is spoken and unwritten — the clearest case of the short-vowel problem
خو here is /xu/ — the same و is /v/ elsewhere, which a grapheme map cannot know

items.source: en.wiktionary.org: Iranian Persian [se.t̪ʰɒː.ɹé] — confirmed as marked

items.note: five syllables from six letters — the one item where letters undercount rather than overcount
items.colloquial: motšakkeram — 4 syllables rather than 5, the /e/ of -te- drops

items.note: carries a ZWNJ (U+200C), which textToVisemes skips — correctly, by accident of being unmapped
items.colloquial: man gošname — گرسنه collapses from 3 syllables to 2

items.note: both خوا clusters are /xâ/: the و is silent in each, and the library rounds the lips for it twice
